title: Last List Item
description: Read an integer n followed by n integers, and print the last value. Valid indices run 0 to n - 1, so the final element is at index n - 1: index n is out of range and crashes. This is a targeted remedial probe for C5-M01 (index-vs-length): confusing the length with the last valid index fails, most sharply on the single-element boundary where index 1 does not exist. Like every EvidencePack, a failure here is observed evidence that can help diagnosis, never a deterministic detection on its own.
constraints: Each of the n values satisfies -1000000000 <= value <= 1000000000
starter_code:
def last_item(nums):
    """Return the last value in nums."""
    # TODO: use index len(nums) - 1, never len(nums)
    raise NotImplementedError


def main():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return
    n = int(data[0])
    nums = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    print(last_item(nums))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
input_format: First line: an integer n. Second line: n integers separated by spaces.
output_format: A single integer: the last of the n values.
